recommendation: Prioritize VTE risk-assessment and prophylaxis protocols for hospitalized patients with a hematologic malignancy who are 75+ and/or male, the groups with the steepest, most significant rate increases.
priority_stakeholders: Hematology/oncology & pulmonology societies; health-system quality officers
supporting_evidence: CDC AAPC NA (NA to NA) %/yr; segmented APC after breakpoint (2014.8): 5.25 (3.45 to 7.07) %/yr; mean AAR 35-54 yrs = 0.06; mean AAR 55-74 yrs = 0.52; mean AAR 75+ yrs = 1.74
caveat: The COVID-era spike (RQ3) may not fully persist; re-estimate as 2025+ data release. The AGE file has no under-35 band.

recommendation: Direct disparity-targeted VTE-prevention education and access programs to the racial groups and geographic regions with the highest and/or most persistent rate ratios; expand reporting for the Asian subgroup.
priority_stakeholders: State health departments; policymakers; hematology/oncology societies
supporting_evidence: Male vs Female: RR 1.60 (1.55 to 1.65) (all years); Black or African American vs White: RR 1.27 (1.21 to 1.33) (all years); Census Region 2: Midwest vs Census Region 1: Northeast: RR 1.13 (1.08 to 1.18) (all years)
caveat: Rate ratios are ecological; Hispanic ethnicity overlaps race; urbanization ends 2020; states_ allows only a two-period comparison.

recommendation: Expand home- and hospice-based end-of-life care capacity and reimbursement pathways to match the observed shift away from inpatient death, and maintain surveillance so that projections and place-of-death shifts are re-estimated as new WONDER years release.
supporting_evidence: largest place-of-death share change: Decedent's home, +8.3 pp (Holm p = 2.88e-35); projected AAR in 2040, Linear trend, 1999-2024: 0.42 (0.31-0.52); projected AAR in 2040, Linear trend, post-Joinpoint 2015-2024: 0.70 (0.51-0.89); projected AAR in 2040, ARIMA(0,1,0): 0.39 (0.15-0.63); projected AAR in 2040, ETS: ETS(M,N,N): 0.39 (0.14-0.64)
caveat: Projections assume no change in VTE prophylaxis, malignancy treatment, or diagnostic practice; intervals are wide; use as planning scenarios only.
